tape.c: -3.5% Tue settle on recovering Middle East exports

tapeLine: US stocks slipped Tuesday as Treasury yields hit fresh multiyear highs: the Dow fell 131.59 points (0.26%) to 51,349.92, the S&P 500 lost 0.16% to 7,670.84 and the Nasdaq Composite eased 0.09% to 26,797.54, per Yahoo Finance and CNBC reports. The 10-year yield climbed to 5.293%, the highest since 2007, and the 30-year to 5.6206%, the highest since June 2002, per a Babypips/Investrade-sourced summary. WTI settled down $3.22 (3.5%) at $89.38 and Brent fell 2.6% to $102.59 as Saudi tanker loadings resumed at Yanbu, per CNBC and Nation Thailand. Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 81.9 in September from a revised 88.6 (consensus in the prior brief: 89.4) and JOLTS openings fell 256,000 to 7.079M in August (prior-brief consensus: 7.23M), per the summary cited. Wednesday futures were little changed to slightly lower ahead of PCE inflation data, per Yahoo Finance.
matters:
Tuesday's session was a bond-led move: the 10-year yield reached 5.293% and the 30-year 5.62%, both multiyear highs, while stocks slipped only modestly, per Yahoo Finance and Babypips. Consumer confidence dropped to 81.9, reported as the weakest since 2014, and job openings fell to 7.079M, both below the consensus figures carried in Tuesday's brief. The Fed-hike thread carried since 18 September stays open with the 28 October FOMC the decision point.

Oil fell 3.5% (WTI $89.38) as Middle East exports were reported at 17.5M barrels a day, 98% of pre-war levels, per CNBC. Iran's foreign minister said he expects a formal US response Tuesday to Tehran's proposal; no response or meeting has been confirmed in sources found, per CBS News and Axios.

Invalidation: Wednesday's 8:30 ET GDP and Personal Income & Outlays (PCE) releases, Thursday's ISM Manufacturing (10:00 ET), Friday's jobs report, any confirmed US response to Iran, and the 10-year yield's behaviour around 5.29%.

regime.tag: Yields made fresh multiyear highs while stocks barely moved and oil fell on recovering Middle East exports.
regime.sizing: The Fed-hike thread stays open, with the 28 October FOMC the decision point. The Iran thread awaits a US response, unconfirmed. Weak confidence and openings data add a growth-side question to the rates thread.

secondOrder: Tuesday reversed Monday's split: oil fell 3.5% and stocks moved little, while yields rose to new highs, so rates again stood out as the driver over crude. Weak confidence alongside rising long yields is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: Tuesday's brief named the 10-year's behaviour around 5.27% as a test. The yield moved through it to 5.293%, per Babypips. Its read that rates rather than crude were the main driver held: WTI fell 3.5% while stocks slipped only 0.16%.
Tuesday's brief carried early Dow futures edging lower. The Dow closed down 0.26%, per Yahoo Finance.

Tuesday's brief flagged JOLTS and Conference Board as tests, with consensus 7.23M and 89.4. Actuals were 7.079M and 81.9, both below. Whether that changes the Fed thread awaits Wednesday's PCE. Resumed US-Iran talks remain unconfirmed.
